title: Where Canada's growth came from
hook: In 1971–72, births minus deaths drove 67% of Canada's growth.
hookNote: Growth here = births minus deaths plus net international migration (immigrants, minus net emigration, plus net non-permanent residents). July to June periods.

beats.text: From here on, international migration added more people than births minus deaths every year.
International migration: +1,108,060, including +703,206 net non-permanent residents. Births minus deaths: +31,829.
Net non-permanent residents: −154,614, the largest outflow in this series since 1971.

Births minus deaths vs net international migration (immigrants − net emigration + net non-permanent residents); shares exclude the published residual (to 2020–21). Components plus residual match population change in every period. 2025–26 is preliminary. Movement between years is animation.
This video shows where growth came from, not why.

raceTitle: Canada: growth by component, each year
sourceLine: Source: Statistics Canada, Table 17-10-0008-01. Movement between years is animation.
method: Printed figures are published Statistics Canada components (or sums/differences of them) for the period on screen. Column heights, province tints (share of growth from international migration, capped at 0-100%) and bars move linearly between periods as animation only. Negative natural increase is drawn as a flat column; its value is printed. 2025-26 is preliminary.
